card: Expands the generateblock RPC to accept multiple coinbase payout destinations with optional custom satoshi amounts, splitting any leftover block reward equally across outputs or burning it to OP_RETURN if no outputs are specified. It also allows omitting the transactions parameter to mine transactions directly from the mempool. This eliminates the need for test harness workarounds when simulating multi-recipient mining pools or generating blocks with mempool transactions. Release notes and CLI argument conversion support are included.
changed_since_previous: Adds release notes and registers the `output` parameter in `vRPCConvertParams` with `ParamFormat::JSON_OR_STRING` to handle single-string or JSON array/object inputs via bitcoin-cli.
evidence: PR description cites an external request from SuperTestnet discussing decentralized mining pool setups requiring multiple coinbase payouts
Commit 9baeea743f and functional test updates eliminate repetitive workaround boilerplate across 11 test suites previously using `output="raw(42)"` or `output="raw(55)"`
problem: Regtest and test harnesses simulating decentralized mining pools or complex payout schemes cannot generate coinbase transactions with multiple payout recipients using standard RPCs. In addition, callers of `generateblock` were previously required to pass explicit transaction lists even when they simply wanted to mine whatever was in the node's mempool, forcing tests to supply dummy outputs and manual transaction queries.

risk.why: Incorrect coinbase reward division or block template weight reservation could produce invalid blocks or fail template generation during regtest and test operations.

scope_notes: Touches both RPC argument parsing and block template construction sizing (reserved weight and sigop calculations for mempool inclusion). Updates numerous functional test files to drop now-unnecessary dummy parameters.
summary: Expands the `generateblock` RPC to accept multiple coinbase destinations with optional explicit satoshi payout amounts, dividing any remaining block reward equally among all outputs. It makes the `output` parameter optional, defaulting to burning the reward in an OP_RETURN output if omitted. It also allows omitting the `transactions` parameter to automatically select and mine transactions directly from the mempool.
